title: E0044: Input-Dependent Runtime Growth
plain_english: Reports loops whose work grows faster than the configured runtime threshold as an input-sized collection grows.
why_matters: Runtime cost that grows superlinearly with input size can cause slow requests, timeouts, or denial-of-service risks when input is large or attacker-controlled. E0044 is part of Phanalist's resource-analysis rules (E0044-E0046), which model allocation, retention, and input cardinality separately from bounded verification rules.
bad_example:
<?php
function hasDuplicates(array $items): bool
{
    foreach ($items as $a) {
        foreach ($items as $b) {
            if ($a === $b) { return true; }
        }
    }
    return false;
}
good_example:
<?php
function hasDuplicates(array $items): bool
{
    $seen = [];
    foreach ($items as $item) {
        if (isset($seen[$item])) {
            return true;
        }
        $seen[$item] = true;
    }
    return false;
}
what_it_checks: Nested loops over the same input-sized collection
Loops that repeatedly perform linear work such as `array_unshift()`, `array_merge()`, `in_array()`, `array_search()`, `preg_match()`, or repeated array copying
Linear work inside a loop that is already linear in the same size measure
Loops whose bound is an unguarded input cardinality, reported together with E0046
Calls to local functions or methods whose resource summary makes the enclosing loop superlinear
